intro.paragraph1: These General Terms and Conditions (the “GTC”) govern the contractual relationship between you as a user (the “User” or “you”) and the provider regarding the use of the handball statistics app “Statix” as well as the associated websites, the progressive web app and the related services (together, “Statix” or the “Service”).

scope.title: § 1 Scope and provider
paragraphs: These GTC apply to the use of Statix in the version valid at the time the contract is concluded. Deviating terms of the User are not recognised unless the provider expressly agrees to their applicability in text form.
Statix is aimed at coaches, players, clubs and handball teams and may be used both by consumers (section 13 German Civil Code) and by entrepreneurs (section 14 German Civil Code).
The provider and contracting party is the operator named below. The full provider identification pursuant to section 5 DDG can be found in the legal notice:

subject.title: § 2 Subject matter and description of services
paragraphs: Statix is a browser-based application (progressive web app) for recording and analysing handball statistics and for organising day-to-day team life. The Service comprises in particular the following functions:
items: Live recording of match events (goals, shots, saves, penalties, substitutions and more) in real time by tapping – including offline in the sports hall, with automatic synchronisation as soon as an internet connection is available again.
Automatic calculation of player and team statistics, shooting percentages, shot charts, heatmaps and development trends.
Management of teams, squads and player information, invitation of further coaches and self-service onboarding of players via an invitation link.
Club level: grouping several teams under one club, joint administration by club administrators and a cross-team career view for a person.
Scheduling: trainings, matches and team events with responses (accept/decline), reminders, absence entries (e.g. holiday, illness, injury) and a subscribable calendar feed (iCalendar).
Browser push notifications for appointments and reminders, provided the User expressly enables them.
Surveys sent to the squad via a link without sign-in.
Creation of tournaments with several teams, automatic standings and fixtures.
Automated, AI-assisted analysis of matches, teams and individual players.
Optional public live coverage of a match (“live ticker”) via an unguessable link, optionally with sponsor logos.
Sharing analyses via link, exporting the match report as a PDF and exporting individual statistics tables as CSV.
paragraphsAfter: Statix is under continuous development and in its market launch phase. The specific scope of functions follows from the current version of the Service and from the service description on the provider's websites. The provider is entitled to further develop, change or adapt individual functions to the extent this is reasonable for the User and the core of the contractually owed service is preserved.
Statix is a tool for documentation and analysis. The provider owes neither a particular sporting result nor the accuracy of the data entered by the User.

registration.title: § 3 Registration, user account and requirements for use
paragraphs: Using the full range of functions requires registering a user account with a valid email address and a password. A non-binding live demo of individual functions is available without registration.

By submitting the registration the User makes an offer to conclude a usage contract. The contract is concluded once the User has verified their email address via the confirmation link sent to them and the provider has activated the account.
The User undertakes to provide truthful and complete information upon registration and to keep it up to date.

Registration is permitted to natural persons who have reached the age of 16. Minors between 16 and 18 may create an account only with the consent of their legal guardians; by registering, a minor User confirms that such consent exists. Persons under the age of 16 are not provided with their own account. They may be recorded as squad members by a coach without holding an account themselves; § 7 applies accordingly.
If the User acts on behalf of a club or an organisation, they warrant that they are authorised to represent it.
Access credentials must be kept secret and protected against third-party access. The User shall inform the provider without undue delay as soon as there are indications of misuse of the account.
There is no entitlement to registration. The provider may refuse to activate an account without giving reasons.

roles.title: § 4 Roles: coaches, players, club
paragraphs: Statix distinguishes several roles with different permissions. For the purposes of the rights and obligations under these GTC:
items: Coaches create teams, record squads and matches and administer the team's data. They decide which data is entered into Statix and which content is published.

Players can create their own account via an invitation link and claim their squad entry. They then see appointments, their own statistics and responses, and can control their own entries themselves – such as absences and whether their name is shown on public pages.
Club administrators manage several teams of a club jointly and can view data across those teams, provided the teams are assigned to the club.
paragraphsAfter: If a team is assigned to a club, the team's data belongs organisationally to the club and not to an individual coach account. If a coach closes their own account, a team with further members continues to exist and is handed over to a remaining member (§ 12 para. 4).

The assignment of a role does not entitle the provider to intervene in the internal relationship between club, coaches and players. Disputes about who may view or change which data are to be resolved between the parties involved.

availability.title: § 5 Availability, maintenance and changes to the Service
paragraphs: The provider endeavours to keep the Service available without interruption but does not owe any particular level of availability. In particular, maintenance work, technical faults, capacity reasons or circumstances outside the provider's control (e.g. force majeure or outages at third-party providers) may lead to temporary restrictions.

Statix is offline-capable. Data recorded while offline is first stored locally on the device and synchronised with the provider's servers once an internet connection exists. A functioning internet connection and a compatible device are required for successful synchronisation. If the device's browser data is deleted before synchronisation has taken place, data not yet transferred is lost.

As the provider is in its market launch phase, further development, adjustments and individual functional changes may occur. The provider will inform the User of material changes in an appropriate manner.

The provider is entitled to discontinue operation of the Service in whole or in part. In the event of permanent discontinuation, the provider will inform the User at least 30 days in advance and give them the opportunity to export their data.

The provider may impose quantitative limits on individual functions (e.g. the number of AI analyses per team and period) in order to ensure stable operation and a fair distribution of capacity. The applicable limits are displayed in the application.

pricing.title: § 6 Free and paid services
paragraphs: The Service is currently provided free of charge. No fees apply for registration or for the functions currently available; there is no payment obligation without an express, separate agreement.

The provider intends to offer paid subscriptions in the future, in particular for teams and clubs. The scope, prices, billing periods and service details of a paid subscription follow from the applicable service and price overview in the ordering process.

A paid contract is only concluded once the User expressly selects a paid service, confirms the price information and completes the ordering process via a button expressly labelled as entailing an obligation to pay (section 312j para. 3 German Civil Code). Before such a contract is concluded, the User is informed of all essential elements of the contract, in particular the total price.

All prices are final prices. The provider charges VAT only to the extent it is obliged to do so; where the small business rule under section 19 German VAT Act applies, no VAT is shown and a corresponding note is included on the invoice.

Existing free accounts do not automatically become subject to charges when paid services are introduced. If a function previously offered free of charge will in future only be available for a fee, the provider will give reasonable advance notice; § 16 remains unaffected.

obligations.title: § 7 User obligations and responsibility
paragraphs: The User undertakes to use Statix only within the framework of applicable law and these GTC.

The User is themselves responsible for all content and data they enter, store or process in Statix. This applies in particular to personal data of third parties, such as players (e.g. names, year or date of birth, jersey numbers, positions, performance data, attendance and absences).

The User warrants that they are entitled to process the personal data of third parties they enter and that they have the necessary legal basis for doing so (e.g. consent or a provision in the club's statutes). Where the data concerns minors, the User must obtain the required consent of the legal guardians.

If the User enters information from which a person's state of health can be inferred – in particular an absence due to illness or injury and any associated notes – they are processing special categories of personal data within the meaning of Article 9 GDPR. For such entries the User must obtain the explicit consent of the data subject in advance, or of the legal guardians in the case of minors. The provider recommends refraining from free-text notes on illness and injury where they are not necessary for training planning.

The User shall indemnify the provider against all third-party claims asserted against the provider as a result of unlawful entry or processing of data by the User, including reasonable costs of legal defence. This does not apply where the User is not responsible for the infringement.

The User is prohibited from posting unlawful, offensive or infringing content, from misusing the Service, from circumventing security mechanisms, from querying the Service automatically to an extent that goes beyond intended use, or from reverse engineering the software, unless this is mandatorily permitted by law.

The provider may block or remove content and temporarily restrict access if there is reasonable suspicion of a material breach of these GTC or of an infringement of rights. The provider will inform the User of this and, where possible and reasonable, give them the opportunity to comment.

dataProtection.title: § 8 Data protection and processing on behalf
paragraphs: The provider processes personal data within the framework of applicable data protection law. Details of the processing of personal data can be found in the privacy policy.

Insofar as the provider processes personal data of third parties on the User's instructions (in particular player, appointment, absence and survey data) which the User enters on their own responsibility, the provider acts as a processor within the meaning of Article 28 GDPR; the controller is the User or their club. For the user account data itself and for the technical operation of the Service, the provider is its own controller.

Upon request to the address stated in the legal notice, the provider provides a data processing agreement pursuant to Article 28(3) GDPR together with annexes on technical and organisational measures and on the sub-processors engaged. Clubs recording data of youth teams should conclude this agreement before entering any data.
To provide the Service the provider engages carefully selected service providers as processors. These include in particular:
items: Supabase – database and file storage services (hosting region Frankfurt am Main)
Vercel – hosting and operation of the websites and the application as well as anonymised reach measurement
Brevo – sending emails (registration confirmations, reminders, contact requests, newsletter)
Anthropic and OpenAI – AI-assisted analyses based on pseudonymised data
The push services of the browser vendors (including Google, Mozilla, Apple) – delivery of push notifications that have been enabled

The provider bases such transfers on an adequacy decision of the European Commission (EU-U.S. Data Privacy Framework) where the respective service provider is certified, and otherwise on standard contractual clauses pursuant to Article 46(2)(c) GDPR. Further information is set out in the privacy policy.
The provider will inform the User in text form at least 30 days in advance of engaging a new sub-processor; the User may object to the change on important data protection grounds.

ai.title: § 9 AI-assisted analyses
paragraphs: Statix offers automated, AI-assisted analyses of matches, teams and individual players. These analyses are produced with the help of third-party services (in particular Anthropic and OpenAI). An analysis is never generated automatically in the background but is always triggered by a deliberate action of the User.

Before transmission to the AI provider, the names of players are replaced with meaningless identifiers (pseudonymisation). The mapping between identifiers and persons does not leave the Service. The privacy policy describes the details.

The results are AI-generated content within the meaning of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (AI Act). They are labelled as such in the application. AI-generated analyses are based on statistical methods and on the data recorded by the User. They may be incomplete, inaccurate or erroneous and serve exclusively for information and support purposes.

The analyses do not constitute a binding recommendation for action and do not replace the User's own assessment and decision. The provider gives no warranty as to the accuracy, completeness or suitability of the AI-assisted results for any particular purpose.

No automated decision-making in individual cases, including profiling, within the meaning of Article 22 GDPR takes place that produces legal effects concerning a data subject or similarly significantly affects them. Whether a player is selected, developed or substituted is decided solely by the coach.
The User is not obliged to use the AI function; the remaining scope of functions is available without it. Upon request the provider will deactivate AI analysis for a team or a club.

publicSharing.title: § 10 Public sharing and shared content
paragraphs: The User may make individual content publicly accessible via an unguessable link – in particular a running live ticker and finished match reports. Without such express sharing, a team's data is accessible only to its members.

Anyone who shares content thereby publishes personal data of third parties and is responsible for doing so. Before sharing, the User must ensure that the players concerned – or their legal guardians in the case of minors – agree to it.

Players with their own account can specify in their settings that their name is not shown on public pages. This decision always takes precedence over a broader team-level setting and cannot be overridden by a coach.

Sharing can be ended at any time; the link is then no longer accessible. The provider has no influence over whether third parties have copied, saved or cached previously public content in search engines.
Sponsor logos uploaded by the User for the live ticker must be free of third-party rights or a corresponding permission to use them must exist. § 7 para. 5 applies accordingly.

ipRights.title: § 11 Rights of use and intellectual property
paragraphs: All rights to the software, the websites, the design, the trade marks, logos and other content of Statix belong to the provider or its licensors.
For the term of the contract, the provider grants the User a simple, non-exclusive, non-transferable and non-sublicensable right to use Statix within the contractually envisaged scope.

The User retains all rights to the content and data they enter. They grant the provider the simple right of use necessary to provide the Service, in particular to store, process, analyse and display such content within the Service. This right of use ends when the respective content is deleted.
The provider may use data in aggregated and anonymised form which does not permit any conclusions about individual persons, teams or clubs in order to improve and statistically evaluate the Service.
The User's content is not used to train AI models of the provider or of third parties.

dataExport.title: § 12 Data export, deletion and account closure
paragraphs: Within the functions provided, the User can share the analyses they have recorded in Statix, export the match report as a PDF and individual statistics tables as CSV, and subscribe to the appointment calendar as an iCalendar feed.

Beyond the export functions available in the application, the provider will, upon request to the address stated in the legal notice, provide the User with the data stored for their account and their teams in a structured, commonly used and machine-readable format. Requests are processed without undue delay and within 30 days at the latest.

The User can delete their account themselves at any time (Settings → Account). Anyone who can no longer sign in should send the deletion request to the email address stated in the legal notice. Deletion is final; there is no restoration and no grace period.

When the account is deleted, teams in which the User is the sole member are deleted, including the associated squad, match, appointment and analysis data. Teams with further members continue to exist and are handed over to the longest-serving remaining member; the same applies to teams assigned to a club.

The User is themselves responsible for exporting any data they need before deletion or before the end of the contract. The privacy policy describes the details and the storage periods for technical logs.

liability.title: § 13 Warranty and liability
paragraphs: Where the Service is provided free of charge, the provider is liable only for damage based on intent or gross negligence, and in accordance with the provisions on gifts.
Otherwise the provider is liable without limitation in cases of intent and gross negligence as well as for injury to life, body or health.

term.title: § 14 Contract term and termination
paragraphs: The usage contract for free use is concluded for an indefinite period and may be terminated by either party at any time without notice, in particular by deleting the user account.

The term, renewal and termination of any paid subscription are governed by the conditions stated in the respective ordering process. Where a paid continuing obligation is offered to consumers, the provider will provide a termination button pursuant to section 312k German Civil Code.

paragraphs: Consumers have a statutory right of withdrawal in respect of paid contracts for digital content or digital services. For the currently free use there is no right of withdrawal, as there is no service against payment.

controllerRoles.title: Who is responsible for what?
controllerRoles.description: Statix is filled with data from two sides. Who is the controller within the meaning of the GDPR depends on which data is concerned:

items.title: We as the provider are the controller
items.description: for your user account data (name, email address, password hash, sign-in times), for the use of our websites, for contact requests and the newsletter, and for technical operation including error logs and abuse protection.

items.title: The coach or the club is the controller
items.description: for all content entered in the app about other people: squad data, match events, appointments, responses, absences, survey answers and sharing. We process this data exclusively on instructions as a processor pursuant to Article 28 GDPR.

items.title: Data processing agreement
items.description: Clubs and teams that record data of their members – in particular minors – can obtain a data processing agreement pursuant to Article 28(3) GDPR, together with annexes on technical and organisational measures and on the sub-processors engaged, by requesting it at our contact address.

items.title: Data subject rights
items.description: Players should address requests for access, rectification and erasure concerning their squad data to their club or coach. If such requests reach us directly, we forward them to the responsible party and support them in fulfilling the request.

legalBasis.title: Relevant legal bases
legalBasis.introLabel: Relevant legal bases under the GDPR:
legalBasis.introText: Below you will find an overview of the legal bases of the GDPR on which we process personal data. Please note that in addition to the provisions of the GDPR, national data protection requirements may apply in your or our country of residence or establishment. Should more specific legal bases be relevant in an individual case, we will inform you of these in this privacy policy.

items.title: Consent (Article 6(1)(1)(a) GDPR)
items.description: The data subject has given consent to the processing of their personal data for one or more specific purposes. We rely on this in particular for the newsletter, for voluntary information from the onboarding survey and for push notifications.

items.title: Explicit consent for special categories (Article 9(2)(a) GDPR)
items.description: Information from which a person's state of health can be inferred – in our case exclusively an absence entered as illness or injury together with its note – may only be processed with the explicit consent of the data subject, or of the legal guardians in the case of minors. Obtaining this consent is the responsibility of the club or of the recording coach.

items.title: Consent of minors (Article 8 GDPR)
items.description: For information society services offered directly to a child, processing based on consent is lawful in Germany only from the age of 16; below that age the authorisation of the holder of parental responsibility is required.

items.title: Performance of a contract and pre-contractual enquiries (Article 6(1)(1)(b) GDPR)
items.description: Processing is necessary for the performance of a contract to which the data subject is party or in order to take steps at the request of the data subject prior to entering into a contract.

items.title: Legal obligation (Article 6(1)(1)(c) GDPR)
items.description: Processing is necessary for compliance with a legal obligation to which we are subject – such as commercial and tax law retention obligations.

items.title: Legitimate interests (Article 6(1)(1)(f) GDPR)
items.description: Processing is necessary for the purposes of the legitimate interests pursued by the controller or by a third party, provided that the interests, fundamental rights and freedoms of the data subject which require the protection of personal data do not override those interests. We rely on this in particular for secure and stable operation, for the prevention of abuse and for anonymised reach measurement.

items.title: Storage on and access to terminal equipment (section 25 TDDDG)
items.description: Storing information on your terminal equipment and accessing it is permitted without consent only where this is strictly necessary to provide a service expressly requested by you (section 25(2) no. 2 TDDDG). We use only such strictly necessary storage; a consent banner is therefore not required.

securityMeasures.title: Security measures
securityMeasures.paragraph1: In accordance with statutory requirements and taking into account the state of the art, the costs of implementation and the nature, scope, circumstances and purposes of processing as well as the varying likelihood and severity of the risk to the rights and freedoms of natural persons, we implement appropriate technical and organisational measures to ensure a level of protection appropriate to the risk.
securityMeasures.connectionLabel: Securing online connections using TLS/SSL encryption technology (HTTPS):
securityMeasures.connectionText: In order to protect the data of users transmitted via our online services against unauthorised access, we use TLS/SSL encryption technology. These technologies encrypt the information transmitted between the website or app and the user's browser, protecting the data against unauthorised access.
measures: Passwords are stored exclusively as a cryptographic hash (bcrypt) and are not visible to us in plain text.
Every database access takes place server-side and is limited to the respective team or club; there is no access to the database from the browser.
All database tables are additionally locked by “row level security” with no permitting rule, so that the public database keys can read no data whatsoever.
Links for password reset and email confirmation are stored only as a hash, are valid for a limited time and are deleted after expiry.
Sign-in, registration and sharing endpoints are protected against automated attacks by counting limits.
Public sharing (live ticker, shared reports) takes place exclusively via randomly generated, unguessable addresses and can be revoked at any time.
Before any transfer to an AI provider, personal names are replaced by identifiers (pseudonymisation).
Technical data that is no longer needed is deleted by an automatic database job that runs daily (see “Storage period and deletion”).

webHosting.analyticsDescription: We use Vercel Analytics and Speed Insights to measure the reach and the technical performance of our website. The analysis works without cookies and without any other storage on your device. From the IP address, the user agent and further technical characteristics of the request, the provider forms a hash value that changes daily and cannot be reversed, in order to recognise repeat visits within one day. The IP address itself is not stored, the hash value cannot be attributed to a person and becomes unusable after 24 hours at the latest. Only aggregated metrics are then evaluated, such as page views, country of origin, device type, browser and loading times (web vitals), as well as two events triggered by us (a click on the live demo and a click on registration).

cookies.title: Cookies and storage on your device

We use exclusively cookies and storage techniques that are strictly necessary for the operation of the service you have expressly requested or that record a setting you have chosen yourself. Neither advertising nor tracking cookies are used. A consent banner is therefore not required (section 25(2) no. 2 TDDDG).

The forms transmit the information you enter to us by email; the form content is not stored in a database. In order to fend off automated mass enquiries, your IP address is kept for a maximum of one hour in a volatile counter in memory and is then discarded.

appSections.title: Data processing in the Statix app
appSections.intro: The following sections describe the processing that takes place when the Statix app (web app and installable progressive web app) is used. Where content is concerned that a coach enters about other people, we act as a processor for the club or team (see “Who is responsible for what?”).

sections.title: Registration and user account
paragraphs: A user account is required to use the app. On registration we process name, email address and password; the password is stored exclusively as a cryptographic hash and is not visible to us in plain text. Voluntary information from the onboarding survey (e.g. league, age group, goals, biggest challenge) is used to improve the offering.

The email address is verified before the first sign-in via a confirmation link (double opt-in). To reset the password we send a link with limited validity by email on request. Both tokens are stored exclusively as a hash and are deleted at the latest seven days after expiry.

Players can also create their own account: the coach shares an invitation link (the team's join link) through which the player claims her own squad entry. The link is valid for 14 days and can be renewed at any time, which invalidates the old link. Who claims which squad entry is decided solely by the player herself; assignment by a coach is not possible.

In order to distinguish active from abandoned accounts, we store the time of the last authenticated use at a resolution of five minutes. This does not create a movement or usage profile; earlier times are overwritten.
You can delete your account yourself at any time (Settings → Account). What is deleted and what remains is described on our account deletion page.

items.label: Types of data processed:
items.value: Master data, contact data, access data, content data, usage data.

items.label: Data subjects:
items.value: Users with their own account (coaches, club officials, players).

items.label: Legal bases:
items.value: Performance of a contract and pre-contractual enquiries (Article 6(1)(1)(b) GDPR); for voluntary survey information: consent (Article 6(1)(1)(a) GDPR); for the activity marker: legitimate interests (Article 6(1)(1)(f) GDPR).

items.label: Storage period:
items.value: Until the account is deleted; tokens for password reset and email confirmation at the latest seven days after expiry.

sections.title: Team, squad and player data
paragraphs: The core function of the app is recording handball match statistics. To this end users create data for their team: first and last name, jersey number, position, goalkeeper flag, period of squad membership and type of membership (regular squad, second squad, guest) as well as match events and the statistics calculated from them (e.g. goals, shots, saves, suspensions, playing times, substitutions). Club details and a club logo can optionally be stored.

To distinguish people with the same name and to determine the age group, the year of birth and – only if the club enters it – the full date of birth can additionally be stored. The year of birth is sufficient for the age group; we recommend not entering the full date of birth where it is not needed.

This data regularly concerns people who do not use the app themselves, including minors. The recording user or their club is the controller: they must inform the data subjects – or their legal guardians in the case of minors – about the processing and, where necessary, obtain their consent. We process this data exclusively on instructions.
The data is visible only to the members of the respective team and – where the team is assigned to a club – to that club's officials, unless a match is expressly shared publicly (see below).

items.label: Types of data processed:
items.value: Master data, master data of squad members, content data, match and statistics data.

items.label: Data subjects:
items.value: Users; players recorded by users, including minors.

items.label: Legal bases:
items.value: The controller is the club or the recording coach; typically consent (Article 6(1)(1)(a) GDPR) or the club's legitimate interests (Article 6(1)(1)(f) GDPR). Our processing takes place as processing on behalf (Article 28 GDPR) on the basis of our contract with the user (Article 6(1)(1)(b) GDPR).

items.label: Storage period:
items.value: Until deletion by the controller, at the longest until the team or the associated account is deleted.

sections.title: Club and cross-team career view
paragraphs: Several teams can be grouped under one club. Club administrators then see the squads and analyses of all assigned teams. Within a club, squad entries of the same person – for example from the under-18 team and from the women's team – can be linked to one person so that a cross-team career becomes visible.

The app proposes such a link on the basis of names, year of birth and membership periods; it is confirmed or rejected exclusively by a human. Rejected proposals are remembered so that the same person is not proposed repeatedly. Linking across club boundaries does not take place.
If a team is assigned to a club, the club can access its data. From that point on, the club is the controller for that data under data protection law.

items.label: Types of data processed:
items.value: Master data, master data of squad members (including year of birth), match and statistics data.

items.label: Data subjects:
items.value: Players recorded by users; club members with their own account.

items.label: Legal bases:
items.value: The controller is the club; our processing takes place as processing on behalf (Article 28 GDPR).

sections.title: Appointments, responses and calendar feed
paragraphs: The app maps the team's calendar: trainings, matches, team evenings and similar appointments with location, meeting time and a note. Squad members accept, decline or answer “maybe” and can leave a comment. Comments are visible only to the coach and to the person writing them, not to the rest of the team. On request the app sends a reminder before an appointment by email or push notification.

The calendar can be subscribed to as an iCalendar feed in a calendar app. The feed is accessible without sign-in via a randomly generated, unguessable address and contains the title, time, location and note of the appointments – but no responses and no names of squad members. Anyone who knows the address can read the calendar; please therefore only pass the link on to people who should have it. The link can be renewed at any time, which invalidates the old link.
The feed is deliberately read-only: responses cannot be given through it, and no attendee lists are transferred into calendar programs.

items.label: Types of data processed:
items.value: Appointment and attendance data, content data (comments, notes), access data (feed token).

items.label: Data subjects:
items.value: Squad members; users with their own account; recipients of the calendar feed.

items.label: Legal bases:
items.value: The controller is the club or the team; our processing takes place as processing on behalf (Article 28 GDPR) on the basis of our contract with the user (Article 6(1)(1)(b) GDPR).

items.label: Storage period:
items.value: Until the appointment, the team or the account is deleted.

sections.title: Absences and health-related information
paragraphs: Squad members can enter longer absences so that not every single appointment has to be declined. An absence consists of a period, a category – holiday, illness, injury or other – and a voluntary note. It can be entered by the person concerned herself or by the coach on her behalf.

If illness or injury is chosen as the category, or if the note contains information about a person's state of health, this constitutes health data and therefore a special category of personal data under Article 9 GDPR. Such information may be processed only with the explicit consent of the data subject – or of the legal guardians in the case of minors. Obtaining and documenting this consent is the task of the club or the coach; we process the information exclusively on instructions.

We expressly recommend either using the category “other” or refraining from free-text notes where training planning does not require the exact cause. The note on an absence is not shown to the other squad members; all they see is that the person is unavailable during that period. An absence can be changed or deleted at any time; the category can subsequently be changed to “other”.

items.label: Types of data processed:
items.value: Appointment and attendance data; health-related information (Article 9 GDPR) where entered; content data (note).

items.label: Data subjects:
items.value: Squad members, including minors.

items.label: Legal bases:
items.value: Explicit consent of the data subject or of the legal guardians (Article 9(2)(a) GDPR), to be obtained by the responsible club; our processing takes place as processing on behalf (Article 28 GDPR).

items.label: Storage period:
items.value: Until deletion by the data subject or the controller, at the longest until the team or the account is deleted.

sections.title: Surveys to the squad
paragraphs: Coaches can send surveys to their squad (e.g. feedback on the season or on training planning). The survey is opened without sign-in via a randomly generated, unguessable address; the person answering selects their name from the squad list.

Answers are therefore attributed to the respective person and are not anonymous to the coach. Anyone who wants to give anonymous feedback should be informed that this attribution exists. A survey can be closed; answers already given are then retained, but no new ones are accepted.

items.label: Types of data processed:
items.value: Content data (answers), master data (attribution to the squad entry), access data (survey token).

items.label: Data subjects:
items.value: Squad members.

items.label: Legal bases:
items.value: The controller is the club or the team; our processing takes place as processing on behalf (Article 28 GDPR).

sections.title: Push notifications
paragraphs: If you enable push notifications for appointments and reminders, your browser creates a subscription and passes us its address (endpoint) at your browser vendor's push service, two associated encryption keys and your browser's identifier (user agent). Without this information delivery is technically impossible.

Delivery is handled by the push service of the respective browser vendor (including Google, Mozilla, Apple). The content of the message is encrypted for your device before it is handed over and cannot be read by the push service; the push service does, however, learn the time of delivery and the identifier of your device subscription. Depending on the vendor, a transfer to third countries may take place.

Enabling notifications is voluntary and can be revoked at any time: you can switch them off in the app settings or withdraw the permission in your browser. Subscriptions reported as invalid by the push service – for example after browser data has been deleted or the app removed – are deleted by us automatically.

items.label: Types of data processed:
items.value: Access data (endpoint and keys of the subscription), meta and communication data (browser identifier, timestamps).

items.label: Data subjects:
items.value: Users with their own account who have enabled push notifications.

items.label: Legal bases:
items.value: Consent (Article 6(1)(1)(a) GDPR; section 25(1) TDDDG); it may be withdrawn at any time with effect for the future.

items.label: Storage period:
items.value: Until unsubscription, until the subscription becomes invalid, or until the account is deleted.

sections.title: Database and file storage (Supabase)
paragraphs: All app data is stored in a PostgreSQL database of the service provider Supabase; club and sponsor logos are stored in the same provider's object storage. Hosting takes place in the EU (Frankfurt am Main region, Germany). Access to the database takes place exclusively server-side; there is no connection to the database from the browser. All tables are additionally locked by “row level security” with no permitting rule.

The provider's parent company is based in the USA, so access from a third country in the course of maintenance and support cannot be entirely ruled out. The guarantees named below are in place for this.

sections.title: Error logs, abuse protection and operational security
paragraphs: To ensure stable operation we store technical error logs. A log entry contains the error message including the technical call path, the address and function affected, the time, the browser identifier (user agent), the version of the application and – where available – the identifier of the signed-in account and of the team concerned. Error logs are deleted automatically after 90 days. In the case of serious errors we additionally send a notification to our own operations address.

To protect against automated attacks (such as guessing passwords or sharing links), we count requests to security-relevant endpoints. Your IP address serves as the counting key; sharing and invitation tokens enter the key only as an irreversible hash value. These counters are deleted automatically after 24 hours at the latest.

For the use of the AI analysis we additionally keep a usage ledger which records, per analysis, the team, the user who triggered it, the type of analysis and the time. It serves to enforce usage limits and is deleted automatically after 400 days.

items.label: Types of data processed:
items.value: Log data, meta, communication and procedural data (including IP address), usage data.

items.label: Data subjects:
items.value: Users; visitors to our online offerings.

items.label: Legal bases:
items.value: Legitimate interests in secure and stable operation (Article 6(1)(1)(f) GDPR).

items.label: Storage period:
items.value: Error logs 90 days; abuse protection counters 24 hours; AI usage ledger 400 days. Deletion is carried out by an automatic database job that runs daily.

paragraphs: Transactional emails – such as the registration confirmation, password reset links, team invitations, appointment reminders, shared match reports and system notifications – as well as emails within the scope of the contact and feedback form and the newsletter are sent via the service provider Brevo. Email address, name and the respective message content as well as technical dispatch information are processed in the course of this.

sections.title: Newsletter
paragraphs: When you sign up for our newsletter we process your email address in order to send you information about Statix. Sign-up takes place using the double opt-in procedure: the address is only added to the distribution list after the link sent by email has been confirmed. Sign-ups and sign-offs are logged for evidential purposes. You can unsubscribe from the newsletter at any time via the unsubscribe link in every email or by sending us a message; we then delete your address from the distribution list.

items.label: Types of data processed:
items.value: Contact data, meta, communication and procedural data.

items.label: Data subjects:
items.value: Newsletter recipients.

items.label: Legal bases:
items.value: Consent (Article 6(1)(1)(a) GDPR); it may be withdrawn at any time with effect for the future.

items.label: Storage period:

sections.title: AI-assisted analyses
paragraphs: At the express request of the user, the app produces AI-assisted analyses of matches, players and teams. The analysis never runs automatically in the background: it is triggered exclusively by a deliberate click of the user.

Before transmission, all player names are pseudonymised. Every player is replaced by a meaningless identifier of the form [[P1]], [[P2]], …; the mapping between identifier and person remains exclusively in our database. Only aggregated match and statistics values (e.g. goals, shots, saves, suspensions, playing times, scores, positions) as well as club and opponent names are therefore sent to the AI providers. Names, dates of birth, jersey numbers, email addresses or photos of players do not leave the app. Only when displayed in the browser are the identifiers replaced again by the real names from your own team's squad.

According to the providers, data transmitted via the programming interface (API) is not used to train their AI models. We store the finished analyses in our database (hosting region Frankfurt am Main) so that they can be called up again; they are deleted together with the associated match, team or user account.

The results are AI-generated content and are labelled as such in the application. No automated decision-making with legal effect within the meaning of Article 22 GDPR takes place – the analysis is an assessment for the coach, and the sporting decision is made by a human. On request we deactivate AI analysis entirely for a team or a club.

items.label: Types of data processed:
items.value: Match and statistics data in pseudonymised form (player names replaced by identifiers); usage data.

items.label: Data subjects:
items.value: Users; players recorded by users (only pseudonymised).

items.label: Purposes of processing:
items.value: Creation of match, player and team analyses at the express request of the user.

items.label: Storage period:
items.value: The analysis remains stored until the associated match, team or account is deleted; the usage ledger is deleted after 400 days.

sections.title: Offline function and local storage on your device
paragraphs: As a progressive web app (PWA), the app can also be used without an internet connection. For this purpose, match and team data as well as app resources are stored locally on your device (the browser's IndexedDB and service worker cache) and synchronised automatically with our servers when a connection is available. This local storage is technically necessary for the offline function (section 25(2) no. 2 TDDDG).

The locally stored data remains on your device until you delete the app or browser data. Please note: if the browser data is deleted before synchronisation has taken place, recordings not yet transferred are lost. On a shared device you should sign out after use so that the locally cached squad data does not remain accessible to others.

items.label: Legal bases:
items.value: Performance of a contract (Article 6(1)(1)(b) GDPR); section 25(2) no. 2 TDDDG (technically necessary storage).

sections.title: Public live match coverage
paragraphs: Users can optionally share a match as a public live ticker. The ticker is then accessible without sign-in via an unguessable link and shows team and player names, jersey numbers, match events and scores of their own team; data of opposing players is not published. Sponsor logos uploaded by the club are optionally displayed.

Sharing is actively initiated by the user, who is responsible for ensuring that the players concerned – or their legal guardians in the case of minors – agree to publication. Players with their own account can specify in their settings that their name does not appear on public pages; only the jersey number is then shown. This decision always takes precedence over a broader team-level setting and cannot be overridden by a coach.

In order to display the current number of viewers and to limit load, we store per viewer a random session identifier assigned to the device, with no personal reference, together with the time of the last request. These entries are deleted when the match ends, and after two days at the latest.
Sharing can be ended at any time; the ticker is then no longer publicly accessible. We have no influence over copies or caches made by third parties while it was shared.

items.label: Types of data processed:
items.value: Content data, match and statistics data, master data of squad members, technical session identifiers of viewers.

items.label: Data subjects:
items.value: Players recorded by users; visitors to the live ticker.

items.label: Legal bases:
items.value: For publication: consent of the data subjects (Article 6(1)(1)(a) GDPR), to be obtained by the responsible club; for viewer counting: legitimate interests (Article 6(1)(1)(f) GDPR).

items.label: Storage period:
items.value: Until sharing ends; viewer session identifiers for a maximum of two days.

sections.title: Shared match reports and PDF export
paragraphs: A finished match report can be shared with another coach. To do so the app generates an unguessable address; on request we additionally send an email to the recipient address specified by the user. Stored in the process are the recipient address, who shared the report, which components are shared (statistics and/or AI analysis), any expiry date and the time it was first opened.

The report can also be saved as a PDF, and individual statistics tables can be exported as a CSV file. For these exports the following applies: once the file has left your device, its further use is beyond our control.
Sharing can be revoked at any time; the address is then no longer accessible.

items.label: Types of data processed:
items.value: Contact data (recipient address), access data (sharing token), match and statistics data, usage data (time of opening).

items.label: Data subjects:
items.value: Recipients of shared reports; players recorded by users.

items.label: Legal bases:
items.value: Performance of a contract (Article 6(1)(1)(b) GDPR); legitimate interests (Article 6(1)(1)(f) GDPR).

items.label: Storage period:
items.value: Until sharing is revoked, until the sharing link expires, or until the associated match is deleted.

sections.title: Live demo without sign-in
paragraphs: At a separate address we provide a demo version in which recording a match can be tried out without registration. The demo works with fictitious sample data. Please do not enter any real personal data there – entries in the demo are not treated as club data and may be reset at any time.

items.label: Legal bases:
items.value: Legitimate interests in presenting our offering (Article 6(1)(1)(f) GDPR).

childrenAndMinors.title: Children and young people
childrenAndMinors.description: Statix is used in youth teams. Special rules therefore apply here:

items.title: Own account only from the age of 16
items.description: An own user account is reserved for people aged 16 and over. Between 16 and 18 the consent of the legal guardians is additionally required. No own account is provided for children under the age of 16.

items.title: Recording without an own account
items.description: Minors can be recorded as squad members by a coach without having an account themselves. The controller for this data is the club – not the child and not us.

items.title: Obligations of the club
items.description: Before the first entry, the club must inform the legal guardians pursuant to Article 13 GDPR and obtain the necessary consent – in particular for health-related absences and for any public sharing (live ticker, shared reports). We provide a model information sheet and a data processing agreement on request.

items.title: Data minimisation
items.description: The year of birth is sufficient for assigning an age group. The full date of birth, photos and free-text notes on state of health should be avoided where they are not necessary for training operations.

items.title: Exercising rights
items.description: Legal guardians can request access to, rectification and erasure of their child's data. Please address such requests to the club or the coach; if they reach us directly, we forward them without delay and support their implementation.

dataSubjectRights.title: Rights of data subjects
dataSubjectRights.description: Rights of data subjects under the GDPR: as a data subject you have various rights under the GDPR:

items.title: Right to object:
items.description: You have the right, on grounds relating to your particular situation, to object at any time to the processing of personal data concerning you which is carried out on the basis of Article 6(1)(e) or (f) GDPR; this also applies to profiling based on those provisions. Where personal data concerning you is processed for direct marketing purposes, you have the right to object at any time to such processing.

items.title: Right to withdraw consent:
items.description: You have the right to withdraw consent given at any time with effect for the future. The lawfulness of processing carried out up to the withdrawal remains unaffected.

items.title: Right of access:
items.description: You have the right to request confirmation as to whether data concerning you is being processed and to obtain access to that data as well as further information and a copy of the data in accordance with statutory requirements.

items.title: Right to rectification:
items.description: In accordance with statutory requirements, you have the right to request the completion of data concerning you or the rectification of inaccurate data concerning you.

items.title: Right to erasure and restriction of processing:
items.description: In accordance with statutory requirements, you have the right to demand that data concerning you be erased without undue delay, or alternatively, in accordance with statutory requirements, to demand restriction of the processing of the data. You can delete your user account yourself at any time (Settings → Account).

items.title: Right to data portability:
items.description: You have the right to receive data concerning you which you have provided to us in a structured, commonly used and machine-readable format in accordance with statutory requirements, or to request its transmission to another controller. In the app you can export analyses as PDF and statistics tables as CSV; beyond that we will provide you with your data in a machine-readable format within 30 days of a request.

items.title: Complaint to a supervisory authority:
items.description: Without prejudice to any other administrative or judicial remedy, you have the right to lodge a complaint with a supervisory authority, in particular in the Member State of your habitual residence, place of work or place of the alleged infringement. The authority competent for us is the Bavarian State Office for Data Protection Supervision (BayLDA), Promenade 18, 91522 Ansbach.

dataSubjectRights.howToText: An informal message to our contact address is sufficient; no particular form is required. We respond without undue delay and within one month at the latest. If your request concerns squad, appointment, absence or survey data, the club or the coach is the controller; in that case we forward your request there and support its fulfilment.
dataSubjectRights.obligationText: Providing your data is neither required by law nor by contract. However, to set up an account we need your name, email address and password; without this information no account can be created and the app cannot be used. All other information is voluntary.

socialMedia.title: Presences on social networks (social media)
socialMedia.description: We maintain online presences within social networks and in this context process user data in order to communicate with users active there or to offer information about us. We point out that user data may be processed outside the European Union in the process and that the networks may create usage profiles based on usage behaviour. No social network content is embedded on our websites; we merely link to our profile. An exchange of data therefore only takes place once you follow the link.

definitions.title: Definitions of terms
definitions.description: In this section you will find an overview of the terms used in this privacy policy. Where terms are defined by law, their statutory definitions apply. The following explanations are intended primarily to aid understanding.

items.title: Personal data:
items.description: Personal data means any information relating to an identified or identifiable natural person; an identifiable natural person is one who can be identified, directly or indirectly, in particular by reference to an identifier such as a name, an identification number, location data, an online identifier (e.g. a cookie) or to one or more special characteristics.

items.title: Special categories of personal data:
items.description: Data that is particularly worthy of protection – such as health data. In Statix such data arises in only one place: when an absence is entered as illness or injury, or when a note contains information about a state of health. Processing it requires explicit consent (Article 9(2)(a) GDPR).

items.title: Processing:
items.description: Processing means any operation or set of operations which is performed on personal data, whether or not by automated means. The term is broad and covers practically any handling of data, be it collection, analysis, storage, transmission or erasure.

items.title: Controller:
items.description: The controller is the natural or legal person, public authority, agency or other body which, alone or jointly with others, determines the purposes and means of the processing of personal data.

items.title: Processor:
items.description: A party who processes personal data on behalf of and on the instructions of a controller without determining the purposes and means themselves. For the squad, appointment, absence and survey data of the teams, we are the processor of the respective club.

items.title: Pseudonymisation:
items.description: The processing of personal data in such a manner that it can no longer be attributed to a specific person without the use of additional information kept separately. Before every AI analysis we replace personal names with meaningless identifiers; the mapping table does not leave our database.

items.title: Master data:
items.description: Master data comprises essential information necessary for the identification and administration of contractual partners, user accounts, profiles and similar assignments.

items.title: Contact data:
items.description: Contact data is essential information that enables communication with persons or organisations. It includes, among other things, telephone numbers, postal addresses and email addresses as well as means of communication such as social media handles.

items.title: Content data:
items.description: Content data comprises information generated in the course of creating, editing and publishing content of any kind.

items.title: Usage data:
items.description: Usage data relates to information that records how users interact with digital products, services or platforms.

items.title: Log data:
items.description: Technical records about the operation of a system – for us in particular error logs with the error message, the function affected, the time, the browser identifier and the program version.

items.title: Match and statistics data:
items.description: All events recorded in connection with a handball match and the metrics calculated from them – such as goals, shots, saves, suspensions, substitutions, playing times and shot positions.

items.question: What is Statix?
items.answer: Statix is a handball statistics app for coaches, clubs and teams. You track a game live with a single tap – goals, shots, saves, penalties and substitutions – and Statix automatically calculates shooting percentages, player and team stats, shot maps and progress over time. Everything can be shared with your team instantly.

items.question: Can I try Statix without signing up?
items.answer: Yes. The live demo is a fully featured version of Statix with real game data: live stats, shot maps and AI analysis right in your browser – no account needed. In two minutes you'll see how Statix works in the gym.

items.question: Which app is best for tracking handball statistics live?
items.answer: Statix is a handball statistics app built specifically for live tracking on the bench. Every action is one tap away, analysis happens automatically, and the app works offline in the gym. It is made for coaches, assistant coaches, clubs and teams at amateur, youth and competitive levels.

items.question: Who is Statix for?
items.answer: Statix is made for handball coaches, assistant coaches, clubs and teams across all divisions – from youth and amateur handball to competitive play. No technical knowledge is required; you are ready to go in minutes.

items.question: Which devices does Statix run on?
items.answer: Statix runs directly in the browser on smartphone, tablet (iPad and Android) and laptop – both on the sideline and for post-game review at home. No app store installation is required.

items.question: Which handball statistics can I track with Statix?
items.answer: You track goals, shots and shooting percentages, saves, fast breaks, technical errors, penalties (2 minutes, yellow, red) and substitutions. From this Statix automatically builds player and team statistics, shot maps, heatmaps and progress trends across the whole season.

items.question: Is there a free handball statistics app?
items.answer: Yes. Statix is currently free with its full feature set — for a single coach as much as for a whole team, with no credit card and no checkout in the app. A subscription will follow later; its price is not decided yet.

items.question: Do I need any technical knowledge?
items.answer: No. Statix is designed so you can track your first game live within minutes. Every action is just one tap away – no training needed.

items.question: Does the app work offline in the gym?
items.answer: Yes. You can track games completely offline. As soon as you are back online, your data syncs automatically.

items.question: Can I share stats with my team?
items.answer: Absolutely. Players and assistant coaches get access to insights, shot maps and progress over time – as a link or PDF export.

items.question: Can parents and fans follow a game live?
items.answer: Yes. Publish your game as a public live ticker and share the link or QR code – perfect for the club chat, your Insta story or the projector in the gym. Anyone with the link follows the score and game flow live in their browser, no account needed. After the game you end the ticker with one tap and the link stops working.

items.question: Can I share games with other coaches?
items.answer: Yes. You give fellow coaches read-only access to a game's stats and AI analysis – via link or email. Shared games appear right in the recipient's Statix inbox. You can also invite assistant coaches to join your team permanently, so you record and analyse together.

items.question: What can I do with player surveys?
items.answer: Ask about availability, feedback or topics like training times: you create the survey in Statix and share a link. Your players pick their name and answer right in the browser – no account needed. You see the results neatly per player or per question, including averages for scale questions.

items.question: What happens to my players' data in the AI analysis?
items.answer: Privacy is built in: player names are pseudonymised before any data reaches an AI – the analysis works with neutral identifiers instead of real names. You can delete AI reports at any time, and you decide which analyses you share.

items.question: How much does Statix cost?
items.answer: Nothing right now: register at app.statix-app.de and track your first game with no commitment and no credit card. Want to look around first? The live demo runs without an account. A subscription will follow later; its price is not decided yet.

items.question: Who is behind Statix?
items.answer: Statix is built by Arkadiusz Weiss – a handball player from Germany who develops the app out of his own experience on the bench. No anonymous tool: feedback from the gym goes straight into development.

items.question: What is Statix?

privacy.title: Handling player data properly
privacy.description: In a club, a rollout rarely fails on what the coaches can do — it fails on this question. So here is the answer in four points.

points.title: Processing on your behalf under Art. 28 GDPR
points.text: The player data your coaches enter is processed by Statix on the club's behalf. A data processing agreement is provided on request; that is precisely the document a data protection officer asks for.

points.title: Pseudonymised before any AI sees it
points.text: Player names are pseudonymised before data reaches an AI. The analysis works with neutral abbreviations, and reports that have been generated can be deleted again at any time.

points.title: Shared links stay revocable
points.text: A match only becomes public when a coach publishes it, and the release can be withdrawn. On the live ticker, player names appear abbreviated by default.

points.title: Processors disclosed
points.text: Which processors are involved – hosting, database, email delivery and the AI providers – is named in the GTC and the privacy policy, together with notes on transfers to third countries.

privacy.closing: The full provisions are in the <terms>GTC (§ 7 data protection and processing)</terms> and in the <privacy>privacy policy</privacy>. For a data processing agreement an email to <mail>{email}</mail> is enough.

objections.title: What gets said on the committee
objections.description: The sentences rollouts fail on. Here they are, with an answer.

items.question: “So what does it cost?”
items.answer: There is deliberately no price tag on this page. A club with twelve youth teams needs something else than a club with two, and a figure that applies to both would be wrong for one of them. Write to us saying how many teams you want to bring in and what you plan to do with it – then you get an offer that fits your club, early enough for your budget planning. For an individual coach, getting started stays free regardless.

items.question: “Our coaches are not technical.”
items.answer: Statix is built for a coach who coaches on the side. Every action is a tap, there is no training session and no setup anyone would have to do for the club. Whoever wants to can start with goals and shots and leave everything else alone. And anyone who wants to look first opens the live demo without an account.

items.question: “But we already have club software.”
items.answer: Probably one for members, fees and departments – and it should stay where it is. Statix does the opposite: what happens on court and in training. Squads instead of a member list, training attendance instead of payment status, shooting percentage instead of an invoice run. The two side by side is the rule, not the exception.

items.question: “We cannot just enter player data anywhere.”
items.answer: Correct, and that is why it is regulated. For player data you enter on your own responsibility, Statix is a processor under Art. 28 GDPR; a data processing agreement is provided on request. Player names are pseudonymised before AI analyses, they appear abbreviated by default in the public live ticker, shared reports can be withdrawn, and which processors are involved is stated in full in the GTC and the privacy policy.

items.question: “And if we stop after one season?”
items.answer: Then you stop. You can export analyses as PDFs and keep them, deactivate shared links again, and the teams stay with their coaches – the club area is a view onto them, not a cage around them.

faq.title: Common questions from clubs
faq.description: What department heads and committees want to know before they roll Statix out in the club.

items.question: What is the Statix club area?
items.answer: A level above the individual teams. In the handball statistics app every squad of a club hangs under one roof: a club overview with results and the table of all teams, a club-wide player list, an analysis with a season comparison, the careers of players across several teams and collected AI analyses. The individual coaches carry on working in their own team as before.

items.question: Which clubs is this worth it for?
items.answer: Above all for a youth department with many teams that wants statistics kept consistently – from the minis to under-18s and on into the senior section. The more teams there are and the more transitions between them, the more the shared standard creates: comparable numbers, continuous player careers and a department head who does not have to ask eight coaches individually.

items.question: What does Statix cost a club?
items.answer: There is no off-the-shelf price tag for that. What a club needs depends on the number of teams and on what you plan to do with it – so after a short enquiry we make you an offer, rather than naming a figure here that would be wrong for most clubs. For individual coaches, getting started stays free, with no credit card.

items.question: How do we get every team into the club?
items.answer: Through a join code. We create the club and give you the code; each head coach enters it in their team settings and thereby belongs. The route deliberately starts from the coach – the team is theirs, so nobody pulls them in from outside. You can regenerate the code at any time.

items.question: Can players be in several teams?
items.answer: Yes. An under-18 player helping out with the women's team is in both squads – each with her own shirt number, her own schedule and her own numbers. Because both squad places belong to the same person, her stages still come together as one career, and nothing is lost when she moves up an age group.

items.question: How do we keep an eye on training attendance?
items.answer: Every team runs its fixtures in Statix: training, matches and everything in between, as a series too. Players accept or decline themselves – through a join link, without a coach app of their own – and enter longer absences such as holiday, illness or injury as a period instead of declining every single date. The coaching staff sees the full attendance list including those who have not replied yet; reasons for declining stay between the player and the coaching staff.

items.question: Who in the club may see which data?
items.answer: There are three roles. Club administration has access to every team in the club, the sporting director reads everything and changes nothing, and a coach can reach the club's teams but carries on working in their own. Anyone without one of these roles does not see the club area.

items.question: How is data protection handled for player data?
items.answer: For the player data you enter, Statix acts as a processor within the meaning of Art. 28 GDPR and provides a data processing agreement on request. Player names are pseudonymised before AI analyses, so the analysis works with neutral abbreviations. In the public live ticker, names appear abbreviated by default – in youth teams they are the names of minors. Processors used and transfers to third countries are named in the GTC and the privacy policy.

items.question: Does Statix replace our club administration software?
items.answer: No, and it is not meant to. Member administration, fees and department organisation stay in your existing software. Statix covers what does not appear there: squads, fixtures and training attendance, live recording of matches and every analysis that comes out of it.

items.question: What happens when a coach leaves the club?
items.answer: The team and its matches remain. The successor gets access through the coaching staff or the club administration; you do not depend on somebody handing over a private file.

items.question: Do our coaches need training?
items.answer: No. Recording is one tap per action, an account is created in two minutes, and joining the club is a code in an input field. Anyone who wants to look first starts the live demo without an account – it runs on real match data in the browser.

items.question: Does it work in halls with no signal?
items.answer: Yes. Matches are recorded offline and sync as soon as the device is online again. Statix can also be installed on the home screen as an app, without the detour through an app store.

items.text: Player cards with values from real matches, stickers for special performances and a tactics board to set the team up. For the kids it is a sticker album – for you it is the squad with numbers behind it.

items.text: In youth handball, playing time is a permanent topic. If you record how often each player shot and how the playing shares fall, you can show something in a conversation with parents instead of defending yourself.

objections.title: What youth coaches rightly object
objections.description: Four objections I had myself – and how I answer them.

items.question: “I have no free hand during the match.”
items.answer: That is exactly why recording is built the way it is: one action is one tap, with no menu and no follow-up question. And you do not have to record everything. Start with goals and missed shots – that is already more than a tally sheet gives you in the end. When it gets hectic, you add actions after the match.

items.question: “For under-14s that is performance thinking.”
items.answer: Depends on what you do with the numbers. If you use them to rank, yes. If you use them to show a child that their training is paying off, it is the opposite. That is why the focus is on development across a season and not on a leaderboard.

items.question: “I am not a software person.”
items.answer: You do not have to be. There is no setup, no training and no manual: create the squad, start the match, tap. Anyone who wants to see it first opens the live demo – without an account, straight in the browser.

items.question: “Does this cost the club money?”
items.answer: Not at the moment. Statix is free to use, with no credit card and no payment process in the app. So you do not need to ask anyone in order to start on Saturday.

faq.title: Common questions from youth coaches
faq.description: From the age group to the conversation with parents.

items.question: From which age group are statistics worth it in youth handball?
items.answer: They become useful where children can understand their own development – from about under-14s. In under-10s and under-8s it is about ball feel and enjoying the game; there it is enough if you keep track for yourself without making the numbers a topic.

items.question: How do I record statistics while I am coaching?
items.answer: With one tap per action. Start by recording only goals and missed shots – that alone gives you the shooting percentage. Everything else you can add after the match, because actions can be edited afterwards.

items.question: How do I show a teenager their development?
items.answer: Through the trend rather than a single match. In Statix you see shooting percentages and values across several matches, plus the player card in the card album. A conversation about a curve pointing upwards works considerably better than one about a bad match.

items.question: Can parents follow the matches?
items.answer: Yes, through the public live ticker. You publish the match, share a link or QR code, and parents see the score and the flow of the match live in the browser – without an app and without an account.

items.question: Is a handball statistics app free for youth coaches?
items.answer: Yes, at the moment Statix costs nothing: no payment process, no credit card, no trial with an expiry date. The live demo even runs without an account at all.

items.question: What do I do with the numbers in training?
items.answer: Connect them with the shot map: if the percentage only drops from one zone, you know what to practise. And raise numbers positively – “from the back court you are at 58 per cent, let us sharpen the jump shots” works better than criticism alone.

howTo.title: How to keep a handball statistic that changes something
howTo.description: The aim is not more numbers but one decision per match you would not have taken without them.

steps.title: Decide what you really analyse
steps.text: Start with three values: goals, shots and turnovers per player. Shooting percentage, attacks and attacking efficiency fall out of those by themselves. Everything else comes once those three are solid – not before.

steps.title: Write your counting rules down
steps.text: The post counts as a shot, a turnover does not, seven-metre throws run separately, and you treat blocked balls the same way all season. Without a written rule the assistant coach records something different from you on the third match day.

steps.title: Record during the match, not afterwards
steps.text: From memory it is above all missed shots and turnovers that go missing – exactly the actions that make your percentages honest. Record live and you have a complete data set at the final whistle.

steps.title: Work out the percentages and place them
steps.text: Compare with your own previous value first, only then with a benchmark table. Under five attempts in a match and thirty across the season you do not comment on a percentage at all.

steps.title: Derive exactly one decision
steps.text: One metric, one training focus, one conversation. Three matches in the same direction are a topic, an outlier is not. After that you start again at step three.

items.question: Which statistics are there in handball?
items.answer: In attack: goals, shots, shooting percentage, attacks, attacking efficiency, turnovers, seven-metre throws and shot positions. In defence: saves, save percentage, goals conceded, blocks and steals. Plus fast breaks and fast-break share, suspensions with the power-play and short-handed record, and across the season the percentage trends, playing shares and the head-to-head record.

items.question: Which metrics should a coach record as a minimum?
items.answer: Goals, shots and turnovers per player. From those three values come the shooting percentage, attacks and attacking efficiency – enough to decide whether your problem is finishing or keeping the ball. Saves per goalkeeper are the next sensible step.

items.question: How do you calculate the shooting percentage in handball?
items.answer: Goals divided by shots, times 100. Seven goals from twelve shots make 58.3 %. Every genuine attempt on goal counts as a shot, including hitting the post or the bar; a turnover without an attempt does not. You keep seven-metre throws separate, otherwise a reliable penalty taker flatters the whole team's percentage.

items.question: What is a good shooting percentage in handball?
items.answer: It depends on the position: at the pivot 65–75 %, from the back court at nine metres 45–55 %, from seven metres 75–85 % and on the fast break 85–95 %. A team shooting percentage above 60 % is a solid value in amateur handball. These are orientation values from practice, not a measured data set.

items.question: How do I record handball statistics during a match?
items.answer: Either with a tally on a prepared sheet with one row per player, or with an app at one tap per action. What matters is that recording happens live: from memory it is above all missed shots and turnovers that go missing, and the percentages come out systematically too good.

items.question: Can I record handball statistics for free?
items.answer: Yes. The Basic tier of Statix stays free forever, including live recording, shooting percentages and analysis; from 1 January 2027 paid tiers are added for the more demanding features. Anyone who would rather start on paper takes the free Excel template. Both without a credit card; the live demo even runs without an account.

items.question: Do I need a second person on the sideline?
items.answer: For goals, shots and turnovers one person who is also coaching is enough. As soon as shot zones, blocks and steals come into it, two people make it considerably cleaner – usually an assistant coach or an injured player does the recording.

items.question: From when are the numbers meaningful?
items.answer: Individual percentages from one match are noise. As a rule of thumb: at least five attempts for a match percentage, around thirty across the season, and for the goalkeeper about eight recorded matches before their own average is worth using as a reference.

items.question: Are there Handball-Bundesliga statistics here?
items.answer: No. This page explains handball statistics and Statix records the data of your own team. Tables and values from the Bundesliga or regional leagues you will find at the leagues and associations themselves.
